scoreboard.what: Takes the last hour seen at midnight and repeats it for all 24 hours of the next day.
scoreboard.why: The laziest possible forecast. It marks the floor.

scoreboard.what: Copies the same hour from yesterday.
scoreboard.why: A simple baseline: tomorrow looks like today.

scoreboard.what: Copies the same hour from exactly one week earlier.
scoreboard.why: A simple baseline that captures the weekly rhythm.

scoreboard.model: Mean of same hour, last 4 weeks
scoreboard.what: For each hour, the average of that same hour over the previous 4 weeks. Nothing is learned.
scoreboard.why: The rule of thumb everything else is compared against.

scoreboard.what: A classic statistical method (exponential smoothing with a weekly pattern), fitted separately for each zone on its last 6 weeks.
scoreboard.why: Checks whether a classic method is enough without machine learning. It scored 48.9, worse than the 4-week mean (36.4).

scoreboard.what: One machine-learning model (LightGBM) trained on all 30 zones together, using recent demand, hour, weekday and holidays.
scoreboard.why: This is the model being tested.

scoreboard.what: A 50/50 average of the LightGBM forecast and the 4-week mean.
scoreboard.why: Checks whether mixing the model with the simple rule beats the model alone. It scored 33.2, worse than LightGBM alone (31.4).
